# 621: Hvor går oljeaksjene videre? Teodor Sveen-Nilsens favorittaksjer

**Feed**: pengepodden-no  
**Published**: 2026-11-26  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Pengepodden ep. 621 features Teodor Sveen-Nilsen, oil analyst at SpareBank 1 Markets. He reviews the Brent spike to about $118 after the Strait of Hormuz closed, and its fall back to about $90. He expects oil and especially gas prices to normalise over the next 6-12 months, using $75/bbl Brent and $10/MMBtu gas as long-term assumptions. His view is cautious: hold slightly less oil than index weight, kept as a Middle East hedge. He prefers Aker BP, IPC, Panoro and DNO, is neutral on Vår Energi and keeps a sell on Equinor because its earnings are at a peak.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 IPCO — IPC | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 85%

Guest's definitive sector favourite for 5 years. Top pick to own over the next 2-3 years.

#### Reasoning

Guest (SpareBank 1 Markets analyst) singles out IPC for its excellent capital allocation through the oil cycle. It balances investment for future production against shareholder returns. Production is mainly in Canada, plus Malaysia and France. It is a buy and the first name he would own for the next 2-3 years despite his normalising oil price view.

#### Sell Triggers

- if capital allocation discipline deteriorates
- if oil prices fall well below the $75 long-term assumption

> *"Ja, da ville jeg hatt IPC, Svensk Holdsselskap, Lunin-gruppen, notert i Sverige."*

---

### 🟢 AKRBP — Aker BP | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Upgraded from neutral to buy the evening before recording. Low gas share means less downside. About 40% production growth should bring dividend increases.

#### Reasoning

With only 5-10% gas exposure, Aker BP is less exposed than Equinor and Vår Energi to the expected steep fall in gas prices. About 40% production growth over the next couple of years should lift dividends at almost any oil price. Operating cash break-even is under $10/bbl. The guest says it is not a doubling candidate.

#### Sell Triggers

- if production growth projects are delayed
- if oil prices fall well below $75

> *"i går kveld oppgraderte vi AKBP fra neutral til kjøp"*

---

### 🟢 PEN — Panoro Energy | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

A top pick in the last sector report that the guest keeps. Well-run small oil company with good deals and sensible management.

#### Reasoning

The guest recommends buying Panoro alongside IPC and Aker BP. He calls it a well-run small oil company that has done many good deals and is backed by sensible people. It is one of his names for the next 2-3 years, with the caveat that the company is small.

#### Sell Triggers

- if deal-making discipline weakens
- if oil prices fall sharply

> *"Jeg synes det er et veldrevet, lite oljeselskap som har gjort mye bra dealer."*

---

### 🟢 DNO — DNO | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Guest is 'fairly constructive' and calls it a joker. Shift from Kurdistan to Norwegian production could re-rate the multiple. P/E under 10.

#### Reasoning

DNO now has close to 100k bbl/d on the Norwegian shelf after deals such as Sval Energi, while its Kurdistan share is likely to fall. Lower risk should justify multiple expansion, and Norwegian institutional sentiment may improve. It is not a top pick on par with IPC. Kurdistan output was near zero in Q2 because of the war.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Kurdistan security disruptions worsen
- if management makes value-destructive deals

> *"Det er NO jeg er ganske konstruktiv til, faktisk."*

---

### 🔴 EQNR — Equinor | **SELL** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Sell rating despite P/E about 6, because earnings are at a peak. Gas-heavy. Mid-cycle value about NOK 300 vs about 450 share price.

#### Reasoning

The guest expects gas prices to fall steeply from 2-3x his $10/MMBtu normal level. At $75 oil and $10 gas, Equinor earns just over $3/share; at its historical median P/E of about 10, that is roughly NOK 300. He says foreign momentum 'tourists' bought on European gas prices, and there is no rush to buy.

#### Sell Triggers

- if gas prices stay structurally high
- if the share falls well below the mid-cycle value of about NOK 300

> *"Ja, vi har fortsatt salt på Ekinor."*

---

### 🟡 VAR — Vår Energi | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Neutral rating. More gas exposure than Aker BP, so more downside as gas normalises.

#### Reasoning

SpareBank 1 Markets keeps Vår Energi at neutral. Its higher gas share than Aker BP leaves it more exposed to the expected gas price normalisation, but the guest is not negative enough to rate it a sell.

#### Sell Triggers

- if gas prices fall faster than expected

> *"vi er fortsatt neutral på vår"*

---
